detector._note: JSON has no comments, and the plugin's readConfig whitelists its keys (advisoryRules / designSystem / ignoreRules / ignoreFiles / ignoreValues / extensions), so the underscore-prefixed keys here are inert and exist only to carry the reasoning. Root cause, evidence and the standing gap: issue #560.
detector._ignoreRulesReason: Both rules read a var() fallback as a bare literal, which is the form DESIGN.md's Borrowed Palette Rule and the whole token scale are built on. Mechanism, in impeccable 4.1.1: the source scan matches a colour with CSS_COLOR_RE and asks isProbablyColorLiteral (detector/design-system.mjs:709-731), whose styleContext test looks only at the text BEFORE the literal and has no var() exclusion, so `color: var(--vscode-charts-green, #89d185)` qualifies; it then passes only the bare matched token to isAllowedColorRaw (:895-899, :628-640), which strips away the very `var(` its own line :631 would have exempted. design-system-radius mis-parses the same way, capturing the fallback tail - the suppressions this file used to carry were for the captured strings '3px)' and '2px)', one per fallback value, growing forever. Measured across packages/alp-webview/src: 53 colour literals sit inside a var() fallback and 3 do not, and all 3 are the sites DESIGN.md itself sanctions. Worth knowing before trusting the rule's value check: the approved palette it loads for THIS repo holds exactly one colour, rgba(128,128,128,0.1), scraped from a token fallback in tokens.css - so almost every colour in the product fails it by construction. That is the noise mechanism, not a check being lost. The radius scale does load correctly (sm 2px / md 3px / lg 8px / xl 10px / full 9999px).
detector._whatReplacesThem: test/webview.cssTokens.test.js, which is var()-aware, runs in CI where this hook does not, and was proved RED against the real pre-fix sites before being relied on. Arms: 'no border-radius bypasses the token scale with a bare literal' (#558) - all five border-radius spellings, a var() that must name a --radius-* token, percentages and zeros exempt; 'no literal colour ships outside a var() fallback' (#559/#560) - hex, rgb/rgba, hsl/hsla, hwb, oklch, oklab, lab, lch and the named colours, with three DESIGN.md-sanctioned declarations allowlisted by file and text; and 'styling written in .ts/.tsx obeys the same two rules' (#560), which covers what a .css-only gate would have missed and the detector did scan - borderRadius and colour-valued keys in JS style objects, plus the shell's own <style> block in src/ideHub/webviewHtml.ts. STANDING GAP, deliberately not papered over: nothing here checks a colour VALUE against a palette. For --vscode-* tokens nothing could, since the host owns those values; for numeric tokens the #557 fallback-agreement arm does check the fallback against the declaration. Re-enable a rule here if any of that stops being true.
detector._verificationNote: Do NOT try to verify a change to this file with `node <impeccable>/scripts/detect.mjs <some .css>`. The standalone CLI resolves the design system by walking up from the target file and stopping at the first ancestor with a project marker and no DESIGN.md (design-system.mjs:591-620); packages/alp-webview/package.json is exactly that boundary, so no design system loads and every design-system-* rule is skipped before any filtering runs. It reports zero findings whether this config is right or wrong. The hook path pins the root to the session cwd instead (hook-lib.mjs:241-259, :1666-1675), which is the repo root, so only the hook sees these rules at all. To check this file, call readConfig + filterFindings from hook-lib.mjs directly.
